- How to turn raw YouTube transcripts (or logs, docs, examples) into prompt/response training pairs

snippet.title: Higgsfield Supercomputer: What This AI Agent Got Right And Where You Still Take Over
snippet.description:
Try Higgsfield Supercomputer here: https://higgsfield.ai/s/mcp-teacherstech-sQukdB

Higgsfield Supercomputer is a new AI super-agent built for people doing creative and brand work. You pick which AI model does the thinking under the hood -- Claude for content creation, GPT, or Gemini -- and the agent is wired into a stack of image and video generation tools plus a set of built-in workflows for different jobs. The cinematic-flow skill handles cinematic ads (which is what I used). There are also workflows for podcast-flow style two-host video podcasts, tv-ad style premium spots, and video-adapt for recreating existing reels frame by frame. Plus UGC, product reviews, and more.
What surprised me was how strong the strategic and written work was -- the brand book, the shot plan, the market research with real citations. The visual generation still has the typical AI tells you'd expect from any AI video generator in 2026, but the orchestration is genuinely impressive. The agent ships an end-to-end loop from one chat.

I gave an AI agent a fake business and asked it to build everything -- the market research, the brand book, the website, a 30-second video ad, and the social media creatives. This is what came back, what worked, what didn't, and three techniques I learned along the way that work in any AI tool, not just this one.

In the video I walk through the whole thing, show you where I had to push back to get better output (you're still the boss with these tools), and explain the three techniques that actually moved the needle:

Reference images for the look -- generate one in another AI tool if you don't have a real one
Ask for the format that handles your content -- text-heavy work wants code, not an image of code
Compare versions and trust your eyes -- sometimes over-constraining AI makes things worse, not better

If you're a small business owner, freelancer, content marketer, or anyone curious about where agentic AI and visual content agents actually fit in real work, this should give you a clear picture without the hype.

snippet.title: NotebookLM + Gemini = Website Builder (Free & No Code)
snippet.description:
We all know Google's NotebookLM is incredible for organizing research and summarizing dense documents. But what if those insights shouldn't just stay in a notebook?

In this tutorial, I’ll show you how to take a stack of complex research (using NASA's Artemis Missions as an example) and turn it into a stunning, interactive, single-page website using Gemini. The best part? We are going to build it, add functional download links, export the file, and publish it live on the internet for free—all without writing a single line of code.

Whether you are building a resource hub for your classroom, organizing project files, or just want to present information in a more professional way, this AI workflow will change how you use your research.

👇 Links Mentioned in the Video:

Google NotebookLM: https://notebooklm.google/

Gemini: https://gemini.google.com/

Netlify Drop: app.netlify.com/drop

Test it with my NotebookLM: https://notebooklm.google.com/notebook/422742fa-7296-4c8e-94a4-7bf3cefbf430

Artemis SLS Specs Demo PDF: https://drive.google.com/file/d/11-j1pxhoyPvwNNkRMKi4dg7KhT0mzpn8/view?usp=drive_link

🤖 Prompts Used in This Video:

Prompt 1: The Blueprint

Act as an expert UX designer and educational technologist. Analyze the attached NotebookLM research and design the architecture for a single-page educational hub about the NASA Artemis Missions. Break the content into logical sections: a compelling 'Mission Overview' hero banner, a 'Deep Dives & Technical Data' section for payloads and engineering specs, and a 'Launch Timeline'. For each section, dictate the heading, the core takeaways to extract from the research, and suggest a specific visual layout. Suggest a space-inspired, modern color palette.

Prompt 2: The Code Generation

Take the structural blueprint we just agreed upon and generate the complete single-page website in a single HTML file. Use Tailwind CSS via CDN. The design language should be clean and technical—deep space blues, stark white text, soft rounded corners, and vibrant accent buttons. Implement a sticky top navigation bar with smooth scrolling to sections. Use responsive CSS flexbox/grid for the technical data cards, and ensure interactive hover states.

Prompt 3: Adding Interactive Elements

Let's make this more interactive. Add a new section just above the footer called 'Downloadable Mission Guides.' Generate a responsive CSS grid of project cards based on the research. Each card needs a placeholder for an icon, a bold title, a brief description, and a high-contrast 'Download PDF' button with a subtle pulse animation on hover.

Prompt 4: Fixing the Download Links

Update the download button for the Space Launch System (SLS) specs. Change the href link destination to this exact URL: https://drive.google.com/file/d/11-j1pxhoyPvwNNkRMKi4dg7KhT0mzpn8/view?usp=drive_link. Keep all the existing Tailwind CSS classes, layout, and hover animations exactly the same.

snippet.title: The Bottleneck Isn't AI. It's You.
snippet.description:
Read the full breakdown https://danieljindoo.substack.com/
The best engineer alive stopped writing code. For business owners, that is not a coding story, it is a warning about where the real bottleneck moved. This breaks down two interviews (Andrej Karpathy and the CEO of Perplexity) and what they mean if you run a company and direct AI agents instead of writing code yourself.

Karpathy hasn't typed a line since December. His job changed from writing code to directing agents 16 hours a day. The Perplexity CEO is selling the same shift as orchestration. Strip the hype and the takeaway for operators is simple: implementation is getting commoditized, so YOU are the slowest part of the system now, and also the only real moat.

What's inside:
- Why directing tasks beat doing tasks (manager capacity)
- Top-down vs bottom-up learning, and why top-down sticks
- The context rot test: a 30-second way to catch your AI quietly forgetting
- Why models are specializing, not merging into one brain
- The OpenClaw fight (Peter Steinberger) and the PewDiePie self-hosted AI moment
- When implementation is free, trust becomes the product
- Jagged intelligence: a PhD and a 10-year-old at the same time
- Where this thesis breaks (physical work, fundamentals)

snippet.title: Neural Networks Explained: Solving the XOR Logic Gate with Backpropagation
snippet.description:
The XOR logic gate is an excellent example of a neural network that can be trained and utilized to solve complex problems. A non-linear decision boundary is needed as the XOR logic gate is not linearly separable. This means that a multi-layer neural network is needed. 

Backpropagation will be used to train the network, and how this is done will be shown with an architecture diagram and with the equations. A numerical example will be provided to show how the equations are solved. 
 
To train the network, 40,000 epochs are run to optimize the weights and biases. The network was trained using both stochastic and batch gradient descent, which resulted in similar solutions.

Adding noise to the input points in conjunction with adding a hidden layer made it so the resulting decision boundary plot was very close to the ideal case.

Video Description: 

How to build a 4-bit computer using individual transistors will be demonstrated and discussed in detail. Parts of the computer include the clock, memory, accumulator register, register B, ALU, and output register. 

An example program will be run where load A, add, subtract, output and halt are executed. The computer will be put in a loop where it will continuously add by two and then subtract by two. 

Understanding how to build a computer at the transistor level is important information that everyone should understand. Please share this video!
